headline: Reproducible open pipelines and accelerated algorithms for sequencing data analysis
label: Sequencing Analysis Tools Infrastructure
summary: Preprints release reproducible pipelines and GPU-accelerated tools spanning single-cell multiome, copy number, ancient DNA and nanopore QC.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the engineering of reproducible, computationally efficient infrastructure for sequencing data analysis. Several preprints package workflows as configurable pipelines: multiomeR provides QC, integration and annotation of single-nucleus RNA+ATAC Epi Multiome datasets, and Streamline CNV is a Nextflow/Docker pipeline for low-pass WGS copy number analysis. Other items target specific algorithmic bottlenecks. G-ALN is a GPU implementation of BWA-aln and indexing for ancient DNA, with output reported as byte-identical to BWA and reported speedups of ~32x for indexing and ~6x overall. RiboTxAlign allocates ribosome footprint multimappers with a two-stage EM over sample-specific references, and T2G converts transcriptome-aligned BAMs to genome coordinates while preserving CIGAR, tags and modification calls. ONT-LibQC adds shallow nanopore QC ahead of deep chromatin assay sequencing. The published HuRef2.0 workflow is the only item reporting a biological result, a near-T2T diploid assembly from ONT simplex reads alone with 23 gapless chromosomes and NG50 of 2.36 Mb.
